messages.subject_clean: Timeseries CSV for one night sleep anylasis
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am working with the Gentactive data (Newcastle polysomnography and accelerometer data by VanHess). I am wondering if I can get a time-series CSV from GGIR to better understand and compare with ground truth. it seems GGIR can only provide time-series csv for 24-hour recording instead of one-night recording for sleep analysis.
since part5 save_ms5rawlevels which belongs to behavioural classes and non-wear with 24 hours data, but i did not get for one night reording.
any clarification would be appreciated.

Kind Regards,
Abdul Haleem

messages.subject: Re: Question/Warning on new default non-wear detection and its implication on SPT detection
messages.subject_clean: Question/Warning on new default non-wear detection and its implication on SPT detection
messages.body_plain:
Hi Pieter,

Thank you for reporting this. May I ask if the actigraph device was initialized with the idle sleep mode turned on? That low variability in the acceleration for such a long time is very unlikely if the devices was being worn. You may also consider increasing the time for the longest windowsize, default is 1 hour (3600 seconds). It seems like some people may deep sleep until ~75 minutes, it is not frequent but still possible. Either way, I think this is quite a specific case which does now allow for evaluation of the nonwear algorithm.

Best,
Jairo

El miércoles, 29 de noviembre de 2023 a las 16:59:25 UTC+1, Pieter-Jan Marent escribió:
> Dear all
>
> After rerunning my dataset with the latest GGIR version (3.0-1), some default settings have been changed. Non-wear detection is now version 2023 which can have some important implications on sleep period detection. The default version of the non-wear window (argument windowsizes) is 1h (3600 seconds) and this long window is now flagged entirely as non-wear (in stead of the 15 min in 2013 version), see vignette or https://www.accelting.com/updates/ggir-release-3-0-0/. It seems like this can lead to potential errors in sleep period time detection. This is a warning/question to further investigate.
>
> To illustrate my concern with a real example of my dataset (wrist-worn actigraph):
>
> One of my participants indicated in their diary that they went to bed at 00.35 (time in bed) and fell asleep at 00.45 (sleep time). Time in bed was used in a sleep log to aid sleep period time detection.
>
> When using the 2013 version of non-wear detection (previously default), sleep onset was found to be at 0:42:00. Which is in line with the visual inspection of the raw data and the diary.
>
> When using the 2023 version of non-wear detection (default in version 3.0-1), sleep onset was found to be at  2:15:00. The reason for this 1,5h difference is that the 2023 version flagged the whole first hour of sleep as non-wear, where the 2013 only found a small portion to be non-wear. Since the argument "ignorenonwear" is set to TRUE (default), SPT detection only started after this non-wear hour. Resulting in this important misclassification.
>
> I have added screenshots from the visual report, but of course checked these findings in the csv files.
>
> And this is not the only case, I have another night where sleep efficiency scores dropped from 96% to 79% because of this change in non-wear classification.
>
> Could someone confirm this? How is it possible that during sleep, non-wear detection is triggered?
>
> Always happy to share my script and the files if needed, but this was more a general warning/question.
>
> Warm regards,
> Pieter-Jan
>
> PS/ on a higher level: any non-wear in this night seems to be a mistake as the participant did not indicate taking it off the device + even if they removed it after falling asleep, you would suspect a clear "wake during the night" when they put the device back on which is not shown in the data...
>
>
>

messages.subject: Re: Timeseries CSV for one night sleep anylasis
messages.subject_clean: Timeseries CSV for one night sleep anylasis
messages.body_plain:
Hi Abdul,

Please try to clarify if you already solved your previous issue before posting new questions: https://groups.google.com/g/RpackageGGIR/c/6S7eCE3mcaw

As for this question, what information do you need in the time series? If it is only acceleration metrics then you can use the time series exported in part 2 with "epochvalues2csv = TRUE". If you need behavioural classification, then you can get the part 5 time series, please note that those are exported with invalid data excluded by default, set "save_ms5raw_without_invalid = FALSE".

Note that if your file does not meet the minimum recording length to be processed by part 5 <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#22_Prepare_folder_structure:~:text=5.13-,Minimum%20recording%20duration,-GGIR%20has%20been>, then part 5 time series would not be available.

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Sleep quality metric?
messages.subject_clean: Sleep quality metric?
messages.body_plain:
Hi GGIR,

I regularly have to 'clean-up' night data from 'half-days' or from nights where the algorithm did not detect bed time very well. I feel like these artefact nights could really affect an analysis and it is very important to remove them. Manually inspecting plots to remove bad 'night' detections seems a bit time consuming, especially with larger data-sets.

Has anyone been working on or thinking about a 'sleep-quality' metric?  Where one column in the sleep outputs to indicate the 'quality' or 'confidence' in the Sleep Period Time (SPT) detection. Low values could be easily filtered out, instead of having to rely on manually inspecting plots and going back to the data?

Some potential rules to help identify 'bad nights' that I was thinking about could be:
Sleep period time <4hr or >12hr
Sleep efficiency <30% or >95%
Some rules on SleepRegularityIndex?
Long term, could even look at the quality of 'sleep_onset' detection and 'wake' detection, but this would probably have to look at epoch or raw data around those detection periods.

For development and testing, would have to manually annotate a dataset with known 'good' and 'bad' SPT detections and then see how well the model can predict.

Any thoughts or insights are much appreciated, this is something I could add to GGIR if we think it is useful.

Disclaimer: I work for ActiGraph, so would probably implement the same thing in our software.

Thanks, Matt

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sleep quality metric?
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Sleep quality metric?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt,

I think there are a couple of sides to this.

In terms of identifying suspicious classifications without using visualisation:
A possible source of misclassification could be that sleep is scattered over the day and the approach of looking for a single Sleep Period Time window then becomes meaningless. In this case GGIR's estimate of time spent in sustained inactivity bouts during waking hours could be a strong indication that the participant did not have a typical night of rest.
Another explanation for misclassifications can be that non-wear somehow either missed and biased the classification or classified when it did not occur in the case of idle sleep mode. On that note see recent thread this <https://groups.google.com/g/RpackageGGIR/c/U0qWaaBLFcU/m/ErcqrKpzAgAJ> recent post, where my question would be whether ActiGraph is used and whether somehow idle sleep mode caused this. To spot that we would need to log whether idle sleep mode occured per night (not done at the moment).

GGIR already ignores nights with low amount of valid data. Further, the users can already filter the output themselves in Excel, R, or whatever they use for post-processing based on any of the criteria you mention. I think it would be hard to come up with a universal recommendation on what defines a suspicious combination of values as this may be very population specific.

Instead, my recommendation to users would be to look out for:
High values in time spent in sustained inactivity bouts during waking hours.
High values in time spent in nonwear.
If idle sleep mode was on in a certain night => We only log this at recording level at the moment, but not at night level yet.
Large difference between guider and final classification of sleeponset and wakeup time => Can be found in QC/part4_nightsummary_sleep_full.csv
Keep an eye out for outliers in any of the part4 variables.

So, I think the choice is whether a general recommendation like the one I am giving here is sufficient (if yes, then it needs to be part of documentation) or whether the user really needs an extra variable to help automate this process at the risk that it makes them lazy and trust the variable without critically reviewing the data for outliers.

In terms of visualisation inspection:
Note that with argument do.visual we can generate a pdf file with visualisations of the overlap between rest periods (sibs) and guider (e.g. sleeplog) with 40 nights per page. If the user provides also argument outliers.only = TRUE then this report is limited to only nights where the difference between estimated sleep onset and wakeup and start and end of the guider is less than X hours, where X is defined by argument criterror. In my experience this works well if users have access to sleep diary. I am not sure how effective it is in order conditions.

Further, I know one group who has developed their own internal Shiny app to inspect and adjust sleep classifications by GGIR, but they have not shared it or not yet at least. I will ask them next time I speak to them whether they are planning to open source it anytime soon.

That said, I agree that it is currently hard to quickly visually inspect time series for many recordings when looking for specific details. The current visualisations either lack detail or provide detail but are displayed in such a way that makes them hard to navigate. Further, with the visualreport that you helped develop we have the limitation that the information visualised is partly calculated only for the visualisation and not directly coming from the GGIR output which introduces a risk for inconsistencies. I think we fixed most issues, but I am not sure we can blindly trust it.

The solution may be to revisit the strategy towards visualising the data and classifications in GGIR, with maybe the following criteria: (1) an accurate reflection of the classification in the rest of GGIR, (2) flexibility to zoom in on details within time series or recordings within a study, (3) zoom out to scan across large numbers of files that meet a certain condition, (4) option to filter based on recording or night-level characteristics, and (5) able to accommodate different data scenarios such as with or without light sensor data and with gravitational units or count units.

I am exploring how to best approach this and hope to avoid duplicating existing open-source tools. Further, if this would be a big development then ideally it should not end up inside GGIR but become a separate tool. Ideally, something that can be sustained by the community and is not limited to GGIR or a specific accelerometer brand or data format. If you have any suggestions then let me know.

Thanks,
Vincent

messages.subject_clean: Assistance Needed: GGIR R Package - Error in Part5 Day Summary QC
messages.body_plain:
Used accelerometer: Movisens (Move 3)

Used GGIR Version: 3.0.1.

Dear all,

I am reaching out to the GGIR community seeking assistance with an issue I've encountered while working with the R package.

During the creation of the Part5 day summary QC, I've run into an error that has proven challenging to troubleshoot. The issue appears to be associated with the loading of data. Specifically, the assignment of the created .RData name consistently lags one ID behind the actual participant (for an example see the picture below).

 Upon closer inspection, removing ID178 temporarily resolves the issue. This has led me to suspect that the problem is rooted in the data associated with this particular participant.

Further investigation revealed that the acc.bin data is missing as a separate entity in the ID178 folder, despite existing in the unisens structure as evident in the .xml data. Interestingly, a separate acc.csv file for this participant is available. I'm wondering if the absence of acc.bin data might be causing the algorithmic discrepancy.

I am reaching out to the GGIR community for insights and potential solutions. Is it feasible to utilize the acc.csv data for ID178 as a workaround? Alternatively, is there a way to independently extract the acc.bin data from the unisens.xml data for this participant?

Note on ID Order: Please bear in mind that the ID order may not align perfectly chronologically due to study dropouts. The correct order should be "176, 178, 181, 183," with ID178 and ID181 missing.

I appreciate your time and expertise, and I'm hopeful that someone within the community might have encountered a similar issue or can offer guidance on resolving this matter.

Thank you in advance for your assistance and if additional information is required to facilitate understanding of this issue, please let me know..

Best regards,

Tim Balder

I'm hoping to find some help with a problem I've encountered using GGIR.

However, in part 5, it does not pick up the sleeplog and reverts to using HDZAC as the guider (see picture below).

I've tried to identify the problem and tried multiple options with the code and tried multiple other things, including renaming the Excel files, renaming the id names, using different idloc options, but none of this seems to solve the problem. The only thing that I noticed is in the ID name, where all ID names are the same (part 2, part 4 and the sleeplog ID name is GAMES01), but in part 5 the ID name changes to GAMES01.csv

If I could get some help with potentially identifying the problem and how I can fix it, that would be most appreciated!

Below I have attached the code and I'm happy to provide full outputs if needed! I appreciate I don't have to write out the full shell function, but wanted to see if I could identify the problem :)

Warm regards,
Lara

In order to run mode 3:5 you need to make sure that the GGIR output folder is the folder you previously used, because this assumed that part 1 and 2 output are present, on which part 3, 4 and 5 rely. I made that suggestion to save you the time of having to reprocess part 1 and 2, but if you deleted the previous output then you have no choice other than to start again.

Regards,

Vincent

Apologies, I'm just coming back this.

I did come across the timezone issue, some of my recordings include the seasonal clock change, however I tried various combinations of configtz and desiredtz with no luck. In addition a re-ran the analysis using an old recording that worked on a previous version of GGIR, that does NOT have a timezone transition, and that was producing the same error. I also tried rolling back GGIR to an older version, with the same results, so it looks to me like it's some interaction of GGIR and the system it's running on. I think I've ruled out conflicts with other R packages by only loading GGIR.

If it helps, my 'workaround' was to do the analysis on an old laptop with the old version of GGIR, so I could run the same file using the same commands on both machines, and compare the output?

Many thanks

Andy

messages.subject_clean: Assistance Needed: GGIR R Package - Error in Part5 Day Summary QC
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tim,

Thank you for the detailed reporting of your issue. At the moment GGIR is able to read MOVISENS bin files, when I implemented this I only had access to bin files, so GGIR expects a file named acc.bin in your participant folder. I guess this is the problem you are facing. The quick solution for you would be skipping the participants without acc.bin as you are doing and try to read those files with the read.myacc.csv function in GGIR <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/readmyacccsv.html>. This is interesting as some years ago movisens did not provide me with a csv file and that's why I had to implement the reading of their bin files.

As for extracting the bin file for these participants, I think you would need to contact Movisens for that.

I am going to try to replicate this issue and make GGIR able to skip the participants in which the acc.bin file is missing. I will get back to you when this is done.

Best,
Jairo

> Dear all,

> During the creation of the Part5 day summary QC, I've run into an error that has proven challenging to troubleshoot. The issue appears to be associated with the loading of data. Specifically, the assignment of the created .RData name consistently lags one ID behind the actual participant (for an example see the picture below).
>
>  Upon closer inspection, removing ID178 temporarily resolves the issue. This has led me to suspect that the problem is rooted in the data associated with this particular participant.
>
> Further investigation revealed that the acc.bin data is missing as a separate entity in the ID178 folder, despite existing in the unisens structure as evident in the .xml data. Interestingly, a separate acc.csv file for this participant is available. I'm wondering if the absence of acc.bin data might be causing the algorithmic discrepancy.
>
> I am reaching out to the GGIR community for insights and potential solutions. Is it feasible to utilize the acc.csv data for ID178 as a workaround? Alternatively, is there a way to independently extract the acc.bin data from the unisens.xml data for this participant?
>
> Note on ID Order: Please bear in mind that the ID order may not align perfectly chronologically due to study dropouts. The correct order should be "176, 178, 181, 183," with ID178 and ID181 missing.
>
> I appreciate your time and expertise, and I'm hopeful that someone within the community might have encountered a similar issue or can offer guidance on resolving this matter.
>
> Thank you in advance for your assistance and if additional information is required to facilitate understanding of this issue, please let me know..
>
> Best regards,
>
> Tim Balder

El miércoles, 13 de diciembre de 2023 a las 10:34:38 UTC+1, Jairo Hidalgo Migueles escribió:
> Hi Tim,
>
> Thank you for the detailed reporting of your issue. At the moment GGIR is able to read MOVISENS bin files, when I implemented this I only had access to bin files, so GGIR expects a file named acc.bin in your participant folder. I guess this is the problem you are facing. The quick solution for you would be skipping the participants without acc.bin as you are doing and try to read those files with the read.myacc.csv function in GGIR <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/readmyacccsv.html>. This is interesting as some years ago movisens did not provide me with a csv file and that's why I had to implement the reading of their bin files.
>
> As for extracting the bin file for these participants, I think you would need to contact Movisens for that.
>
> I am going to try to replicate this issue and make GGIR able to skip the participants in which the acc.bin file is missing. I will get back to you when this is done.
>
> Best,
> Jairo
>
> El domingo, 10 de diciembre de 2023 a las 20:13:28 UTC+1, Tim Balder escribió:
> >
> > Used accelerometer: Movisens (Move 3)
> >
> > Used GGIR Version: 3.0.1.
> >
> > Dear all,
> >
> > I am reaching out to the GGIR community seeking assistance with an issue I've encountered while working with the R package.
> >
> > During the creation of the Part5 day summary QC, I've run into an error that has proven challenging to troubleshoot. The issue appears to be associated with the loading of data. Specifically, the assignment of the created .RData name consistently lags one ID behind the actual participant (for an example see the picture below).
> >
> >  Upon closer inspection, removing ID178 temporarily resolves the issue. This has led me to suspect that the problem is rooted in the data associated with this particular participant.
> >
> > Further investigation revealed that the acc.bin data is missing as a separate entity in the ID178 folder, despite existing in the unisens structure as evident in the .xml data. Interestingly, a separate acc.csv file for this participant is available. I'm wondering if the absence of acc.bin data might be causing the algorithmic discrepancy.
> >
> > I am reaching out to the GGIR community for insights and potential solutions. Is it feasible to utilize the acc.csv data for ID178 as a workaround? Alternatively, is there a way to independently extract the acc.bin data from the unisens.xml data for this participant?
> >
> > Note on ID Order: Please bear in mind that the ID order may not align perfectly chronologically due to study dropouts. The correct order should be "176, 178, 181, 183," with ID178 and ID181 missing.
> >
> > I appreciate your time and expertise, and I'm hopeful that someone within the community might have encountered a similar issue or can offer guidance on resolving this matter.
> >
> > Thank you in advance for your assistance and if additional information is required to facilitate understanding of this issue, please let me know..
> >
> > Best regards,
> >
> > Tim Balder
> >
> >

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

The custom code that I generated based on this thread has worked well, but I see that at some point you implemented the "study_dates_file" parameter. Could you simply verify that when used with a csv file denoting the start and end dates of expected wear, that the end result will only reflect data collected within this window (based on the masking parameters set in tandem), thus accomplishing the goals laid out earlier in this thread?

I see here (https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/4e33a636599759e438f36fa0c76ace0165d71235/R/g.impute.R#L99) that the function is called within g.impute(), but could you also quickly comment on which part of GGIR this will run in? In other words, will it save me time in part1 for files with many days outside of expected wear?

Thank you,
Tom

On Monday, May 18, 2020 at 8:26:15 AM UTC-6 Tom Kraft wrote:
> Hi Vincent,
>
> I really appreciate the suggestions. This seems reasonably straightforward and it would allow me to fun part 1 in parallel, which seems to be important for runtime. If the code works I'll share it here so others have a workaround if anyone faces the same issue. I'll make sure to remove the extra timestamp column as suggested. If you have any other thoughts in the meantime please do let me know! Best,
>
> Tom
>
> On Monday, May 18, 2020 at 9:22:55 AM UTC-5, Vincent van Hees wrote:
> > ... actually the following step I mentioned is only to help you to identify which timestamps are not of interest to you should be labelled as non-wear:
> > " Create an extra timestamp column in object M$metalong by converting the timestamps to POSIX value with GGIR function iso8601chartime2POSIX."
> > After you have done this, it is best to remove the new timestamp column, just in case the rest of the GGIR gets confused about seeing more columns than expected.
> >
> > Vincent
> >
> > ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐ Original Message ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐
> > On Monday, May 18, 2020 4:17 PM, Vincent van Hees <v.va...@movementdata.nl> wrote:
> >
> > > I think the quickest work around is to process the data with GGIR part 1 as you would normally do. Next, you will have to write an R script that does the following:
> > > - Load the milestone (RData) files generated by GGIR part 1 as stored in the meta/basic folder.
> > > - Create an extra timestamp column in object M$metalong by converting the timestamps to POSIX value with GGIR function iso8601chartime2POSIX.
> > > - Change the non-wear score column in object M$metalong to 3 for all values outside your time interval of interest.
> > > - Save all object you found in the milestone file back to the same file, including the now modified object M.
> > > - Continue with part 2 with default settings for strategy. All time outside your value of interest will be treated as accelerometer non-wear time.
> > >
> > > The other approaches you suggest are not going to work I think.
> > >
> > > Good luck, Vincent
> > >
> > > ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐ Original Message ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐
> > > On Monday, May 18, 2020 3:54 PM, Tom Kraft <kraf...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >
> > > > Hello Vincent,
> > > >
> > > > Thank you for the help and reply. Unfortunately as a postdoc I don't have any funding that could be put towards this cause, so I will likely be stuck with workarounds for now. But I do have two ideas:
> > > >
> > > > 1) The function g.cwaread() is already designed to subset data based on a datetime (ymd hms) for beginning and end of data collection. Because g.shell.GGIR() is internally calling g.cwaread() (based on looking into the source code on github), it seems like it might be straightforward to implement a strategy 4 that only works for this filetype but utilizes the already built in arguments "start" and "end". I tried to figure out how to implement this but I can't seem to figure out where internal arguments are passed to g.cwaread(). In either case though, it doesn't appear that this would require additional functionality?
> > > >
> > > > 2) An alternative approach would be if I could load data with g.cwaread(), which currently works fine, and then feed that object into g.shell.GGIR. It seems like this should be possible but I can't figure out how to do this. I'm not used to working with hierarchical functions that do things like load and analyze data all in one step, so it's possible that I'm missing an obvious way to feed in data that has already been loaded into the environment.
> > > >
> > > > Is there a chance that one of these approaches would offer a very quick solution? Thank you!
> > > >
> > > > Tom
> > > >
> > > > On Thursday, May 14, 2020 at 2:51:54 PM UTC-5, Tom Kraft wrote:
> > > > > Hi,
> > > > >
> > > > > Thank you for this excellent software! I'm new to the GGIR package, but have read through the tutorial, package documentation, and have searched the archives on this group. I am working with cwa data collected with AX3 axivity units and have 2 basic questions:
> > > > >
> > > > > 1) When using g.shell.GGIR(), the vignette tells me that "strategy" in combination with "hrs.del.start" and "hrs.del.end" can be used to subset incoming data by removing a certain number of hours from the beginning and end of the total file (the documentation describes it as how many hours after start of the experiment did wearing of the monitor start). In my experiment, however, I simply started the units some time in advance and noted the time at which wearing began. So in order to calculate the number of hours, I would have to extract the start time from the unit, calculate the number of hours between that time and when wearing started, and then enter that value here from processing. This can be done, but I feel like I must be missing an easier option to simply state the actual timestamp at which wearing started. Is this possible?
> > > > >
> > > > > 2) The first issue caused me to look into the function g.cwaread(), which I believe works under the hood for g.shell.GGIR. In this case, I can directly specify a start and end time point for reading data in "year-month-day hr:min:sec" format. This works, but I am having trouble understanding the function of the "desiredtz" argument in g.cwaread(). My data were collected in the UTC+08 timezone, and thus I do the following:
> > > > >
> > > > > ac1 <- g.cwaread(fileName = "myfile.cwa",
> > > > >           start = as.POSIXct("2020/03/02 17:00:00", tz= "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"),
> > > > >           end = as.POSIXct("2020/03/05 08:20:00", tz="Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"))
> > > > >
> > > > > However, I am surprised to see that this gives me a different output than if I specify desiredtz directly:
> > > > >
> > > > > ac2 <- g.cwaread(fileName = "myfile.cwa",
> > > > >           start = as.POSIXct("2020/03/02 17:00:00", tz= "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"),
> > > > >           end = as.POSIXct("2020/03/05 08:20:00", tz="Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"), desiredtz = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur")
> > > > >
> > > > > I originally assumed that these would give me the same output because the devices were synced to this same timezone when they were configured and collected data. So it is unclear to me what exactly that argument is doing. The package documentation says to see g.getmeta() for details on this argument, but that only gives a link to a webpage with timezones. Could anyone comment on which of the above two approaches is appropriate?
> > > > >
> > > > > Thank you!
> > > > >
> > > > > Tom Kraft

> > > > > UC Santa Barbara

messages.subject: Part 5 inconsistencies - Repeated date with different window_numbers
messages.subject_clean: Part 5 inconsistencies - Repeated date with different window_numbers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone, I hope all is well!

I'm using GGIR (version 3.0-0, R version 4.3.1) on a Mac (M1).
We have used the simple sleep log as the sleep duration/time guider and set the maximum number of days at 7. (maxdur = 7)

Checking the day-level output of part 5, we've noticed many duplicated rows for which the window_number == 8 and calendar date was the same as window_number == 2. (Examples attached)
All the information apart from window_number is identical in these rows.
Interestingly, for most participants with this issue, window_number == 7 was ignored, and the night_number for window_number == 8 is 2.

I've checked for problems in part 4's day-level output (part 4_nightsummary_sleep_full), which seems fine. It includes data for each of the 7 nights.

Has anyone had a similar trouble? It seems there might be a problem when incorporating of part 4 data when calculating part5 output.

I really appreciate any help you can provide.

Regards,
Danilo

Hi Jairo,

Thank you very much for your quick answer and your continued support!

I could resolve the error by excluding the individual with missing data, effectively eliminating the issue. To incorporate the ID into the complete dataset, I am going to utilize the "read.myacc.csv" function. messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom,

The study_dates_file parameter was indeed recently added, and is one of the ways GGIR part 2 allows for specifying what time segment(s) of the recording it should ignore (mask) from further analysis. Other arguments such as hrs.del.start are used on top of this and will apply relative to the dates window as specified.

As a result, part 1 will not be affected and will always read and pre-process the entire recording. I am aware that computationally this is not efficient for recordings with a lot of time to be masked. However, I implemented it in the current way because:
Most studies I have worked with do not have this problem as their sensors are typically worn from the first till the last recording day.
Processing all data in a file offers a complete overview of the recording and ensures no data is skipped that could have been used.
However, if you think it could help to have a GGIR option to only read and process the expected time window then that is technically possible to build. However, I would then need funding for my time to work on that. If you see opportunities for that then please pm me.

Best wishes,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Part 5 inconsistencies - Repeated date with different window_numbers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Danilo,

Duplicate dates are possible in part 5 if argument timewindow is set to "WW" or "OO" because the date reflects the date on which a window starts, and when defining windows from wakeup-wakeup or sleeponset-sleeponset it is possible for two windows to start on the same date, e.g. 1am and 11:30pm within a single day.

However, your screenshot looks more suspicious as entire rows are duplicated. Can you confirm that this is not a duplicated file with a different name that produces the exact same result?

If not, could you send me the corresponding RData file from the meta/basic folder and your R script or config.csv file such that I can reproduce the error in order to investigate closer?

Thanks,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in part3 file NA Filename not recognised
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Error in part3 file NA Filename not recognised
messages.body_plain:
Hi Margaret,

This sounds like GGIR part 3 is trying to process part 2 output data (milestone data) but cannot find them. This could be due to incorrectly specified path or part 2 not producing any output. For example, when forgetting to update the file path after moving data around  on your drives or when re-using R scripts for multiple studies.

So, you may need to break it down in substeps:
If you only run GGIR part 1 and 2 does part 2 then produce the expected output?
If you isolate a small subsample of files and processing those with do.parallel = FALSE does that work? and how about setting do.parallel = TRUE?

Best regards,

Vincent

Hi Vincent,

Thank you for clarifying how this parameter is used! I will run some comparison checks today for consistency. With the updated GGIRread package, the loss of efficiency on part 2 vs part 1 isn't an issue for me, and I agree that implementing there would expose the possibility of erroneous data loss.

Thank you again,
Tom

On Mon, Dec 18, 2023 at 5:22 AM Vincent van Hees <v.va...@accelting.com> wrote:
> Hi Tom,
>
> The study_dates_file parameter was indeed recently added, and is one of the ways GGIR part 2 allows for specifying what time segment(s) of the recording it should ignore (mask) from further analysis. Other arguments such as hrs.del.start are used on top of this and will apply relative to the dates window as specified.
>
> As a result, part 1 will not be affected and will always read and pre-process the entire recording. I am aware that computationally this is not efficient for recordings with a lot of time to be masked. However, I implemented it in the current way because:
> Most studies I have worked with do not have this problem as their sensors are typically worn from the first till the last recording day.
> Processing all data in a file offers a complete overview of the recording and ensures no data is skipped that could have been used.
> However, if you think it could help to have a GGIR option to only read and process the expected time window then that is technically possible to build. However, I would then need funding for my time to work on that. If you see opportunities for that then please pm me.
>
> Best wishes,
>
> Vincent
>
> Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
>

In other words, will it save me time in part1 for files with many days outside of expected wear?

> > > > > I think the quickest work around is to process the data with GGIR part 1 as you would normally do. Next, you will have to write an R script that does the following:
> > > > > - Load the milestone (RData) files generated by GGIR part 1 as stored in the meta/basic folder.
> > > > > - Create an extra timestamp column in object M$metalong by converting the timestamps to POSIX value with GGIR function iso8601chartime2POSIX.
> > > > > - Change the non-wear score column in object M$metalong to 3 for all values outside your time interval of interest.
> > > > > - Save all object you found in the milestone file back to the same file, including the now modified object M.

Hi Lara,

I wasn't able to reproduce your issue. I used GGIR version 3.0-0 and run part 5 only with the definition of the loglocation and it went well:

library("GGIR")
GGIR(datadir = "...",
           outputdir = "...",
           mode = 5, overwrite = TRUE,
           loglocation = ".../Lara_Full sleep log games only 01.csv")

I think the problem is that you accidentally removed part of the definition of your loglocation, in your script I can see:

loglocation = "C:/Users/name/location + excludefirstlast = FALSE

There is part of the path to the sleeplog missing and the closing quote is not there, probably GGIR couldn't find any sleeplog if you run part 5 after removing this part of the script. It helps if you make the effort to clean up the script a bit, there are many arguments in their default values and many other that are not coherent (e.g., you state dataformat = "actiwatch_csv" and then you provide all the rmc arguments, which doesn't make sense). It took some time to go over your script and find the arguments I was looking for (those related to the sleeplog).

Best,
Jairo

messages.body_plain:
Hi Natã,

Regarding the output, you can get the output in part 2 of GGIR even if participants did not wear the accelerometer during sleep. And even parts 3, 4 and 5 can work with that data. If the output is reliable or not would be something not directly related to GGIR but to your protocol, consider participants forget wearing the accelerometers after wake up, then you would be missing a part of their day which might influence the average acceleration. This is something that affects all the protocols and outputs from studies based on collecting data only during awake time.

As for you other question, GGIR is now able to read some epoch aggregates from actiwatch and ukbiobank, but actigraph agd format is not one of file format that GGIR can read at the moment.

Best,
Jairo

messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent,
  I'm using GGIR 2.7-1  to analyze my ActiGraph csv data (14 days of monitoring). However, as we know, the file's header doesn't have the participant ID, so the sleeplog id can't match with the participant ID. In consequence, I failed to use the sleeplog to analyze the sleep part.
  Is there any way to solve this problem?

Here is my code:

mode = c(1,2,3,4,5)
datadir = "E:/mystudy/mydata/BPM123.csv"
outputdir = "E:/results"
studyname ="BPM123"
f0 = 1
f1 = 2
GGIR(#-------------------------------
     # General parameters
     #-------------------------------
     mode = mode,
     datadir = datadir,
     outputdir = outputdir,
     studyname = studyname,
     f0 = f0,
     f1 = f1,na.rm = TRUE,
     overwrite = FALSE,
     do.imp = TRUE,
     print.filename = FALSE,
     storefolderstructure = FALSE,
     rmc.headername.recordingid = NULL,
     #-------------------------------
     # Part 1 parameters:
     #-------------------------------
     windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
     do.cal = TRUE,
     do.enmo = TRUE,
     do.anglez = TRUE,
     chunksize = 1,
     printsummary = TRUE,
     #-------------------------------
     # Part 2 parameters:
     #-------------------------------
     strategy = 1,
     hrs.del.start = 1,
     hrs.del.end = 1,
     maxdur = 0,
     includedaycrit = 16,
     M5L5res = 10,
     winhr = c(5,10),
     qwindow = c(0,24),
     mvpathreshold = c(100,120),
     #-------------------------------
     # Part 3 parameters:
     #-------------------------------
     timethreshold = 5,
     anglethreshold = 5,
     ignorenonwear = TRUE,
     #-------------------------------
     # Part 4 parameters:
     #-------------------------------
     excludefirstlast = FALSE,
     includenightcrit = 16,
     nnights = 14,
     loglocation = "E:/mystudy/sleepdiary/sleeplog.csv",
     outliers.only = FALSE,
     relyonguider = FALSE,
     colid = 1,
     coln1 = 2,
     do.visual = TRUE,
     sleeplogidnum = FALSE,
     #-------------------------------
     # Part 5 parameters:
     #-------------------------------
     # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
     threshold.lig = c(30,40,50),
     threshold.mod = c(100,120),
     threshold.vig = c(400,500),
     boutcriter = 0.8,
     boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,
     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
     boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
     boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,20,30),
     boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),
     boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),
     timewindow = c("WW"),
     #-----------------------------------
     # Report generation
     #-------------------------------
     do.report = c(2,4,5))

Best,
Chan

messages.subject: Inquiry regarding data merging
messages.subject_clean: Inquiry regarding data merging
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey released the physical activity monitor raw data of 2011-2014 in October, 2022. It is .csv format derived from ActiGraph GT3X+.

Here is the website: https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Nhanes/2011-2012/PAX80_G.htm
In NHANES 2011-2012 cycle, accelerometry data is available for 6,917 participants 6 years and older. The current release (PAX80_G) consists of 6,917 zipped archive files – one for each participant. Due to the very large quantity of the data, these files are stored at the CDC File Transfer Protocol (FTP) Server. The number such as “62161” in the first picture is the number of one participant.

Each participant may have up to 194 hours of accelerometer measurement records. I downloaded the first zipped archive files, which contains the accelerometry information of one participant called “62161”. After the decompression, there are many hourly accelerometer files and one log file aiming to quality control. Each file contains the hourly accelerometry information of this participant. I hope to merge all .csv file as shown in the second picture into one .csv file every time I use GGIR to cope with accelerometry data. I hope to know whether GGIR has this function to merge the information from all .csv file into one .csv file, or whether GGIR can cope with hourly accelerometry information and have the output?

Kind Regards,

Jane.

messages.body_plain:
Margaret,

I did some testing and I think I figured out what caused the warning  you reported,

"Warning messages: 1: In filesummary[vi:(vi + 6)] <- c(file_summary$Dur_imputed, file_summary$Dur_chsum_failed, : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length 2: In filesummary[vi:(vi + 6)] <- c(file_summary$Nblocks_imputed, file_summary$Nblocks_chsum_failed, : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length"

I just sent a pull request addressing this issue, so we'll probably have this fixed soon.

As for why some of your files were reported as corrupt / too short in GGIR 3.0-1 but not in GGIR 3.0-2 -- my guess is that these files have some corrupt blocks in them. I'm guessing that when you were upgrading GGIR you also upgraded GGIRread to the latest 0.3.2, which now imputes corrupt Activity cwa blocks. In the past these blocks were identified as corrupt but still processed, potentially leading to unexpected errors. Since now these blocks are imputed, the file overall doesn't need to be treated as corrupt and can instead be processed normally. messages.body_plain:
Dear Danilo,

Thanks for your reply, I am cc-ing back the ggir google group and removed the link to your dataset in your email.

Ok, I reprocessed your example files with

GGIR(mode=2:5,
     datadir = "...",
     outputdir= "...",
     overwrite = TRUE,
     do.report = c(2, 4, 5),
     do.parallel = TRUE,
     timewindow = c("MM", "WW"),
     windowsizes=  c(1, 900, 3600),
     desiredtz = "America/Sao_Paulo")

Note that you had "ovewrite", which is a typo by which you were not actually overwriting the previous results.

This then produces part 5 report files without duplicated entries. However, when I look at the visual report pdf files I see that the angle time series can impossibly represent wrist data. It seems you are using GGIR for a sensor location that is not wrist without making an effort to tailor the input arguments to this new sensor location. As a result, the sleep classifications do not make much sense.

That in itself does not explain the duplicated nights yet in your output. So, I started reinserting some of the arguments you used and see that dayborder = 20 causing the duplicated days. My quick impression is that dayborder no longer works for part 5, after the introduction of qwindow to part 5 earlier this year.

I was not using dayborder myself and will have a look whether this can be fixed.

Best,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Danilo,

You are not specifying which sleep detection algorithms you want to use: You may want to set HASPT.algo = "HorAngle" as that will detect the longest period of being horizontal. Note that sleep detection within the SPT window is not likely to be reliable as all of the available sleep/wake classifiers are developed for wrist.  However, HorAngle should at least provide you to isolate waking hours from bedtime hours.

Some of this is described in the vignette, but I agree that documentation needs improvement... hopefully next year we make progress on that.

To try out a possible fix I just prepare for the dayborder issue, please install GGIR development version via:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue1006_dayborder_part5")

Cheers,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Part 5 inconsistencies - Repeated date with different window_numbers
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Part 5 inconsistencies - Repeated date with different window_numbers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

You are not specifying which sleep detection algorithms you want to use: You may want to set HASPT.algo = "HorAngle" as that will detect the longest period of being horizontal. Note that sleep detection within the SPT window is not likely to be reliable as all of the available sleep/wake classifiers are developed for wrist.  However, HorAngle should at least provide you to isolate waking hours from bedtime hours.

Thank you for the explanation. As you pointed out, for my projects the most useful feature of part 5 is discerning wake from bedtime.

A couple more points to check if I understood correctly:
 - When the sleep log is available, the sleep window will be assumed to be the sleep log onset and wake.
 - For participants without sleep log data, the HorAngle algorithm will try to catch the longest time of being horizontal and assume this is bedtime.
 - In both cases, this period will be named SPT, and SPT start/end should be pretty reliable (at least for those with the sleep log).
 - The variables within this window (e.g., MVPA and sleep duration during SPT) are probably unreliable and should not be interpreted due to the accelerometer placement (as I expected).

Some of this is described in the vignette, but I agree that documentation needs improvement... hopefully next year we make progress on that.

If there's anything I can do to help with this, please let me know.

To try out a possible fix I just prepare for the dayborder issue, please install GGIR development version via:
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue1006_dayborder_part5")

I've ran the same code with this updated version of GGIR.
I've noticed that previously the start_end_window was registered as 00:00:00-19:59:59, but now it is correctly registered as 20:00:00-19:59:59.
The issue seems to have been fixed, but I'll check it more carefully and report back to you.

Cheers!
Danilo
